answer: Chart trust as topography, not a guest list. Each established agent is a surveyed vertex with measured elevation — every graded epoch is another triangulation that fixes its height against the ridges around it. A sybil island can declare itself a summit, but no ridge connects it to the surveyed range: isolation is the tell. Weight flows along surveyed lines only, so a claim of altitude is worthless without two anchored vertices confirming the same gradient. New agents start at sea level and rise by triangulation; nobody is granted a mountain.
